result:
Assuming PostgreSQL. Expand-only: adds and backfills the new columns and leaves `full_name` in place, so the migration is safe to re-run and old code keeps working.

```sql
-- migrations/0042_split_full_name.sql
-- Idempotent: re-running is a no-op once the backfill is done.
BEGIN;

ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name text;
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name  text;

DO $$
BEGIN
  -- Guard: full_name may already be dropped by a later contract migration.
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_schema = current_schema()
      AND table_name = 'users' AND column_name = 'full_name'
  ) THEN
    -- First token -> first_name, the rest -> last_name.
    -- ponytail: naive split; "Mary Ann Smith" gives first="Mary", last="Ann Smith".
    -- Names don't split cleanly. Keep full_name as the source of truth if that matters.
    UPDATE users
    SET first_name = substring(full_name from '^\s*(\S+)'),
        last_name  = substring(full_name from '^\s*\S+\s+(.*\S)')
    WHERE first_name IS NULL
      AND last_name  IS NULL
      AND full_name IS NOT NULL
      AND btrim(full_name) <> '';
    -- ponytail: single UPDATE that locks touched rows for its duration.
    -- On tables with millions of rows, batch by id range instead.
  END IF;
END $$;

-- Self-check of the split logic. Aborts the transaction if it is wrong.
DO $$
BEGIN
  ASSERT substring('  Ada Lovelace ' from '^\s*(\S+)') = 'Ada';
  ASSERT substring('  Ada Lovelace ' from '^\s*\S+\s+(.*\S)') = 'Lovelace';
  ASSERT substring('Cher' from '^\s*\S+\s+(.*\S)') IS NULL;
  ASSERT substring('Mary Ann  Smith' from '^\s*\S+\s+(.*\S)') = 'Ann  Smith';
END $$;

COMMIT;
```

Why it is re-runnable:
- `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` makes the schema changes no-ops on a second run.
- `WHERE first_name IS NULL AND last_name IS NULL` means the backfill never overwrites rows that were already split or edited by the app.
- The `information_schema` guard means it won't fail after `full_name` has been dropped.

Skipped:
- Dropping `full_name` and adding `NOT NULL`. Put these in a separate contract migration once app writes go to both columns.
- Batched backfill. Add it when the table is large enough that row locks matter.
- Trigger-based dual-write. Add it if old app versions keep writing `full_name` during the rollout.
